title: Give your company's knowledge assistant a phone number

steps.text: Most companies now have an internal knowledge assistant. Ours is called Atlas. It answers questions from our docs, tickets and dashboards.
But our people often need answers away from a screen. Driving to a customer, or walking into a meeting.
A phone version is a second product: speech, phone numbers, checking who's calling. That's weeks of work.
And a simple voice wrapper just reads the answer aloud, citations and all.

Here's what I found. Acme Retail. Renewal date, March twelfth. Source one, open bracket, C R M slash accounts slash acme dash retail, close bracket. Open tickets, three. Ticket four four eight one two.
{{product}} gives any text agent a real voice, and a phone number.
It sits between people and their agents. It listens, keeps answers short, asks before it acts, and calls back when there's news.
To give Atlas a voice and a phone number, I add three lines of code. Atlas doesn't change.
It reads what Atlas can do, checks who's calling, and speaks for it. Now anyone at the company can call it.
Hi Atlas. I'm meeting Acme Retail in twenty minutes. Anything I should know?

Three things. Their contract renews in March. They have one open issue: settlements have been a day late since last Tuesday. And their payment volume is up eighteen percent this quarter. Want details on the delay?
Not yet. The fix ships Thursday, and no money was lost. Their contact, Dan, was told on Friday.
Okay. Can you get me their volume by region? I want it for the meeting.
That needs a fresh query on the dashboards. It takes a minute or two. I'll call you back.
Hi Priya, it's Atlas. West is up thirty-one percent, and it's driving most of the growth. The other regions are flat. I've texted you the chart and the sources.
Same Atlas, same code. Now everyone can call their company's knowledge, from anywhere.
